subject: Usage-tier anchoring & reseller netting for CloudScale private offer
messages:
From: Alex Kim <alex.kim@cloudscale.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cloudscale.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace private offer — usage tiers and reseller netting

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the demo last week — team liked the throughput and cost story. Procurement asked for a bit more color before we move to signatures:

1) Usage-tier anchoring: we need to understand how list-price anchors behave over the first 12 months. If we commit to a 3-tier usage schedule (0-1M, 1M-5M, >5M tokens), can you confirm whether Redwood will hold list price on the lower tiers for renewal / repricing purposes, or if those anchors reset at renewal?

2) Reseller netting: we plan to purchase via our reseller partner. They expect the private-offer invoice to net to Redwood's list price (so they can apply their margin). Will Redwood provide a disclosed netting workflow or should we model the reseller split off-invoice? Any examples or previous templates would help.

3) Shelf-life on discounts: our procurement policy requires clarity on how long a quoted discount in a private offer is guaranteed once the PO is issued.

If you can share a short note and example numbers (or a sample private-offer PDF) that walks through these three items, we can align with procurement and legal.

Appreciate it — can we target EOD Friday for an answer?

Best,
Alex
CloudScale — Head of Cloud Procurement

Attachments: none

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Kim <alex.kim@cloudscale.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — usage tiers and reseller netting

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick answers below and I attached a short worked example and our standard private offer terms. Happy to hop on a 30-min call if you want to walk numbers.

1) Usage-tier anchoring: anchors are fixed for the contracted term. Example: if you commit to Tier 1 pricing for year 1 (0–1M tokens) and actually consume 1.8M, the overage pricing applies but the anchor for renewals remains the contracted Tier 1 anchor unless we agree a new offer at renewal. In short: anchors do not automatically rebase at renewal.

2) Reseller netting: Redwood issues the invoice to the buyer on the private offer; reseller margins are typically applied off-invoice by our partners. We can support an explicit "netting" line on the invoice in special cases, but it requires a reseller addendum and a billing flow change (and is typically allowed for strategic partners only). For CloudScale's case, we can propose a pass-through flow where the reseller invoices the customer and Redwood recognizes revenue at net price — this needs a short reseller addendum.

3) Discount shelf-life: quoted discounts on a signed PO are guaranteed for 30 days after PO issuance for private offers, unless otherwise noted in the offer terms. We can extend this to 60 days for multi-year commits on a case-by-case basis.

Next steps: I attached
- private_offer_terms_v2.pdf (terms + reseller addendum template)
- redwood_marketplace_anchor_and_netting_20270822.pdf (worked numbers + invoice examples)

If that matches what procurement needs I can loop in Ben (sales ops) and Lauren (pricing) to finalize the reseller addendum language. Would you prefer a short call Tues/Wed next week?

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: private_offer_terms_v2.pdf (pdf), redwood_marketplace_anchor_and_netting_20270822.pdf (pdf)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Marketplace private offer — usage tiers and reseller netting

Alex / team — thanks for the patience. Pricing/RevOps reviewed the example and we can proceed with the following positions:

- Anchor behavior: confirmed — anchors remain as contracted for the term. We will include a plain-language clause in the private offer PDF that clarifies anchor preservation at renewal unless both parties sign a replacement agreement.

- Reseller netting: we can support an explicit netting invoice in the private-offer flow for strategic reseller relationships. Requirements:
  • Signed reseller addendum (attached template)
  • Reseller must be a registered channel partner with Redwood (partner ID on file)
  • Minimum lead time of 15 business days to change billing flows to netting (billing ops window)

- Discount shelf-life: standard guarantee is 30 days after PO issuance. For multi-year commits (>=2 years) we can extend to 60 days; extension requires legal sign-off and inclusion in the offer metadata.

I attached an updated private offer PDF that:
- Displays a sample 3-tier usage table with list and net invoice examples
- Contains editable reseller addendum language for CloudScale
- Includes a note on billing cutover lead times

Next actions:
1) Alex — confirm reseller partner ID and whether CloudScale prefers on-invoice netting (Redwood invoices CloudScale net of partner margin) or off-invoice pass-through.
2) Soojin — if Alex confirms, prepare a draft private offer, include reseller addendum, and set billing lead time date (15 business days after signature).

Happy to jump on a 20-min call to finalize wording.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Pricing & Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
